docs.title: The Lynch Team SOP
docs.text:
Standard Operating Procedures for The Lynch Team

This site is the single source of truth for how we run things. It's searchable (press /), mobile-friendly, and has a dark mode.

docs.title: Pick a Procedure
docs.text:
• Email Marketing — Weekly Blast

    Weekly email process. Two paths: New Listing or Blog.

    Open SOP

  • Social Media Video Publishing

    Publish 1 video per day. CapCut → AI content → Facebook / IG / TikTok / YouTube / Stories.

    Open SOP

  • GoHighLevel Management

    Automations, contact cleanup, website, page building, funnels, QC.

    Open SOP

  • Website Management

    Content audits, SEO, Open Graph, publishing QC.

    Open SOP

docs.title: Suggesting a Change
docs.text:
Every page has an edit pencil in the top-right corner. Click it, make your change, and open a pull request. The site updates automatically once merged.

New to the team?

Start with GoHighLevel Management — it's the system everything else runs on.

docs.title: Email Marketing - Weekly Email Blast
docs.text: Frequency: Weekly Platform: GoHighLevel (GHL) Owner: (add name) Last reviewed: (add date)

docs.title: 1. Trigger
docs.text:
Begin the weekly email marketing process by checking whether a qualifying new listing is available for promotion.

Decision Point

Is there a qualifying new listing available?

  • YES goes to Path A: New Listing Email Blast
  • NO goes to Path B: Blog Email Blast

Only one path is completed for each weekly email blast.

docs.title: PATH A - New Listing Email Blast
2. Pull Listing Information
docs.text:
1. Open the property listing in MLS.
  2. Pull the required property information from the MLS listing.
  3. Use the MLS listing as the source of truth for property information.

docs.title: 3. Generate Email Content
docs.text:
1. Run the MLS listing details through AI.
  2. Generate the property highlights and email draft.
  3. Proofread the AI-generated email.
  4. Compare the email against the MLS listing.
  5. Correct any information that does not match the property.

docs.title: 4. Build Email in GHL
docs.text:
1. Open the GHL Email Builder.
  2. Add the approved email copy.
  3. Download the required property photos from OneDrive.
  4. Upload the photos to GHL Media Storage.
  5. Add the photos to the email.
  6. Add the required property information and links.
  7. Review the completed email.

docs.title: 5. Configure Tracking
docs.text:
Add the required action-based tracking tags:

Tag Trigger / Action marketing email Contact opened email email Contact unsubscribed hardbounced Email hard bounced softbounced Email soft bounced click marketing Link clicked fb Facebook link clicked ig Instagram link clicked linkedin LinkedIn link clicked

docs.title: 6. Configure Batch Sending
docs.text: Setting Value Receiver Tag Buyers Batch Quantity 300 contacts Batch Interval 15 minutes Sender Name (add required sender name) Sender Email (add required sender email) Schedule Date (add scheduled date) Schedule Time (add scheduled time)

docs.title: 7. Dimitrios Review
docs.text:
1. Send the email draft to Dimitrios for review.
  2. Review his requested changes.
  3. Update the email as needed.
  4. Repeat revisions if necessary.
  5. Once the final email is approved, proceed with the batch email.

docs.title: 8. Send and Monitor
docs.text:
1. Process the approved batch email for sending.
  2. Check email statistics periodically.
  3. Monitor:
    • Send/delivery quality
    • Opens
    • Link interactions
    • Unsubscribes
    • Hard bounces
    • Soft bounces
  4. Monitor the campaign until sending is complete.
  5. Confirm the campaign finishes without errors or unusually high bounce activity.

docs.title: PATH B - Blog Email Blast
docs.text:
Info

Use this path only when there is no qualifying new listing available for the weekly email blast.

docs.title: 2. Select Social Post
docs.text:
1. Select one existing social media post to use for the weekly email marketing content.
  2. Determine the intended audience for the content:
    • Buyer
    • Seller
    • Other applicable audience

docs.title: 3. Build and Publish Blog Post
docs.text:
1. Build a blog post based on the selected social media content.
  2. Develop the blog around the content's intent and target audience.
  3. Add an appropriate CTA based on the blog's intent.
  4. Review the completed blog post.
  5. Publish the blog post.
  6. Confirm the published blog post is accessible.

docs.title: 4. Generate Email Content
docs.text:
1. Run the completed blog post through AI.
  2. Generate the email blast draft.
  3. Proofread the email.
  4. Confirm the email matches the blog post's intent and content.
  5. Correct any inaccurate or unsupported information.

docs.title: 5. Build Email in GHL
docs.text:
1. Open the GHL Email Builder.
  2. Add the approved email copy.
  3. Add CTA buttons directing recipients to the blog post.
  4. Create a video-style thumbnail with a play button.
  5. Link the thumbnail to the blog post.
  6. Review the completed email and links.

docs.title: 6. Configure Tracking
docs.text:
Add the required action-based tracking tags:

Tag Trigger / Action marketing email Contact opened email email Contact unsubscribed hardbounced Email hard bounced softbounced Email soft bounced click marketing Blog Post link clicked fb Facebook link clicked ig Instagram link clicked linkedin LinkedIn link clicked website Website link clicked

docs.title: 7. Configure Batch Sending
docs.text: Setting Value Receiver Tag Buyers Batch Quantity 300 contacts Batch Interval 15 minutes Sender Name (add required sender name) Sender Email (add required sender email) Schedule Date (add scheduled date) Schedule Time (add scheduled time)

docs.title: 8. Dimitrios Review
docs.text:
1. Send the email draft to Dimitrios for review.
  2. Review his requested changes.
  3. Update the email as needed.
  4. Once the final email is approved, proceed with the batch email.

docs.title: 9. Send and Monitor
docs.text:
1. Process the approved batch email for sending.
  2. Check email statistics periodically.
  3. Monitor: delivery quality, opens, link interactions, unsubscribes, hard bounces, soft bounces.
  4. Monitor the campaign until sending is complete.
  5. Confirm the campaign finishes without errors or unusually high bounce activity.

docs.title: Weekly Decision Flow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Weekly Email Marketing Trigger] --> B[Check for qualifying new listing]
    B --> C{New listing available?}
    C -->|YES| D[PATH A: New Listing Email Blast]
    C -->|NO| E[PATH B: Blog Email Blast]
    D --> D1[MLS] --> D2[AI Draft] --> D3[Proofread] --> D4[GHL Email] --> D5[Photos] --> D6[Tracking] --> D7[Batch Setup] --> D8[Dimitrios Review] --> D9[Approval] --> D10[Send] --> D11[Monitor]
    E --> E1[Select Social Post] --> E2[Build Blog plus CTA] --> E3[Publish] --> E4[AI Email Draft] --> E5[Proofread] --> E6[GHL Email] --> E7[CTA and Thumbnail] --> E8[Tracking] --> E9[Batch Setup] --> E10[Dimitrios Review] --> E11[Approval] --> E12[Send] --> E13[Monitor]

docs.title: GoHighLevel Management
docs.text:
Owner: (add name) Last reviewed: (add date)

Standard Operating Procedure for managing GoHighLevel (GHL): automations, contact management, website, page building, funnels, QC, and escalation.

docs.title: 1.1 Monitor Existing Automations
docs.text:
Trigger: Ongoing GHL automation management.

  1. Review current GHL automations.
  2. Check automation execution records.
  3. Identify failed, incomplete, or unexpected executions.
  4. Investigate the cause of the error.
  5. Fix the automation as needed.
  6. Test the corrected automation.
  7. Confirm that the automation is executing as intended.

docs.title: 1.2 Build New Automations
docs.text:
Trigger: A task inside GHL can be automated.

  1. Identify the task or process that may benefit from automation.
  2. Discuss the automation idea with Dimitrios.
  3. Determine:
    • What the automation should accomplish.
    • What process the automation should serve.
    • What should trigger the automation.
    • What steps the automation should execute.
    • What conditions or decisions need to be included.
    • What the expected final result should be.
  4. Finalize the automation workflow with Dimitrios.
  5. Build the automation in GHL based on the finalized process.
  6. Test-run the automation.
  7. Verify that each step executes in the correct order.
  8. Confirm that the automation produces the intended result.
  9. Add fallback steps for situations where the automation fails or cannot complete an action.
  10. Monitor the automation after activation and correct issues as needed.

docs.title: 1.3 Automation Requirements
docs.text:
Every automation should have:

  • A defined trigger.
  • A defined sequence of actions.
  • Conditions or decision points where necessary.
  • A defined expected outcome.
  • A fallback process for failed execution.
  • A test run before being activated.

docs.title: Monthly Email Marketing List Cleanup
docs.text:
Trigger: Monthly

  1. Review the current GHL contact database.
  2. Build/update the email marketing list.
  3. Exclude contacts with hard-bounced emails.
  4. Exclude contacts marked as DNC (Do Not Contact).
  5. Verify the resulting list is suitable for email marketing.
  6. Use the cleaned list for future email marketing campaigns.

Purpose: Maintain a cleaner email marketing audience and reduce delivery issues during email campaigns.

Open Item

Define whether other exclusions should be applied, such as unsubscribed contacts, invalid email addresses, or other suppression lists.

docs.title: 3.1 Universal Elements
docs.text:
1. Review website pages for elements that can be saved as universal elements.
  2. Convert applicable repeated elements into universal elements.
  3. Check similar elements across all pages.
  4. Replace duplicate elements with the appropriate universal element where applicable.
  5. Confirm that future changes to universal elements can be applied consistently across the site.

docs.title: 3.2 SEO and Metadata
docs.text:
Review all website pages and confirm they have:

  • Meta tags
  • Open Graph information
  • SEO keywords

Update missing or incomplete metadata as needed.

docs.title: 3.3 Branding
docs.text:
1. Review website pages for branding consistency.
  2. Use the established Lynch Team brand colors throughout the site.
  3. Check similar elements across pages for consistent branding.
  4. Correct inconsistent colors or styling where needed.

docs.title: 4. Page Building
docs.text: Trigger: A new website page needs to be created or an existing page needs to be edited.

docs.title: 4.1 Planning
docs.text:
1. Coordinate with Dimitrios to determine:
    • Page purpose
    • Page content
    • Page layout
    • Required sections
    • Required CTAs
    • Intended audience
  2. Confirm the page direction before building.

docs.title: 4.2 AI-Assisted Draft
docs.text:
1. Use AI to develop the initial page draft.
  2. Generate or assist with visual concepts where needed.
  3. Optimize page content for:
    • SEO
    • AEO
    • AI searchability
  4. Review the generated content against the intended purpose of the page.
  5. Make necessary revisions.
  6. Present the draft for approval.

docs.title: 4.3 Build in GHL
docs.text:
Only after the draft is approved

  1. Build the page inside the GHL Page Builder.
  2. Add the approved content.
  3. Add the approved layout and visual elements.
  4. Add required CTAs and links.
  5. Apply Lynch Team branding.

docs.title: 4.4 SEO and Metadata
docs.text:
Add:

  • Meta tags
  • Open Graph information
  • SEO keywords

docs.title: 4.5 Review and Publish
docs.text:
1. Review the completed page with Dimitrios.
  2. Apply requested revisions.
  3. Recheck page content, layout, links, and metadata.
  4. Once approved, publish the page.
  5. Confirm the published page is functioning correctly.

docs.title: 5. Funnel Building
docs.text: Trigger: A new funnel needs to be created or an existing funnel needs to be edited.

docs.title: 5.1 Planning
docs.text:
1. Coordinate with Dimitrios to determine:
    • Funnel purpose
    • Page content
    • Page layout
    • Target audience
    • Required CTAs
    • Lead capture requirements
    • Form/survey requirements
    • Lead workflow after form/survey submission
  2. Determine how leads should enter and move through the funnel.
  3. Confirm the funnel structure before building.

docs.title: 5.2 AI-Assisted Draft
docs.text:
1. Use AI to develop the initial page draft.
  2. Generate or assist with visual concepts where needed.
  3. Optimize page content for:
    • SEO
    • AEO
    • AI searchability
  4. Review the generated content against the funnel's purpose.
  5. Make necessary revisions.
  6. Present the draft for approval.

docs.title: 5.3 Build Funnel Pages in GHL
docs.text:
Only after the draft is approved

  1. Build the funnel page(s) inside the GHL Page Builder.
  2. Add the approved content and layout.
  3. Add required forms/surveys.
  4. Add CTAs and required links.
  5. Apply Lynch Team branding.
  6. Add meta tags, Open Graph information, and SEO keywords.

docs.title: 5.4 Build Funnel Workflow
docs.text:
1. Create the workflow for leads entering through the funnel.
  2. Define the trigger based on the form/survey submission or other agreed funnel entry point.
  3. Build the workflow according to the process finalized with Dimitrios.
  4. Configure the required actions, conditions, tags, notifications, or follow-up steps.
  5. Add appropriate fallback steps for automation failures.
  6. Test the workflow before activation.

Reference

Follow the Automation Building process in Section 1 when creating or modifying the funnel workflow.

docs.title: 5.5 Review and Publish
docs.text:
1. Review the completed funnel with Dimitrios.
  2. Test:
    • Page functionality
    • Forms/surveys
    • Buttons and links
    • Lead submission
    • Workflow trigger
    • Workflow actions
    • Follow-up process
  3. Apply requested revisions.
  4. Once approved, publish the funnel.
  5. Perform a final live test.
  6. Confirm that submitted leads enter the correct workflow and that the funnel operates as intended.

docs.title: 6. General GHL Quality Control
docs.text:
Before considering a GHL task complete:

  • Confirm the requested process was followed.
  • Verify pages, forms, funnels, and automations function correctly.
  • Test new or modified automations before activation.
  • Confirm required SEO and metadata elements are present.
  • Confirm branding is consistent.
  • Confirm fallback processes exist for automations.
  • Review completed work with Dimitrios when approval is required.
  • Monitor newly activated automations and workflows for execution errors.

docs.title: 7. Escalation and Coordination
docs.text:
Coordinate with Dimitrios when:

  • The intended process is unclear.
  • A new automation requires a workflow decision.
  • Page or funnel content is not defined.
  • A workflow requires a business-rule decision.
  • An automation repeatedly fails after troubleshooting.
  • A requested change would significantly alter an existing workflow.
  • Approval is required before publishing or activating a process.

docs.title: Social Media Video Publishing
docs.text: Process: Publish 1 video per day Frequency: 5 videos per week Primary Trigger: Dimitrios sends video(s) for publication Owner: (add name) Last reviewed: (add date)

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Prepare, publish, document, and temporarily store Lynch Team social media videos using the established workflow.

Editing Rule

CapCut edits are limited to captions, Lynch Team branding, specified on-screen elements, audio adjustment, and thumbnail creation. Do not otherwise alter Dimitrios' original video content unless specifically instructed.

docs.title: 1. Video Intake
docs.text:
Trigger: Dimitrios sends a video for publication.

  1. Retrieve the video.
  2. Confirm the video is intended for social media.
  3. Proceed directly to CapCut editing.
  4. Use the date assigned in the Notion Social Media Planner for the post.

Important

Dimitrios sending the video is the trigger to begin the publishing workflow. Do not wait for a separate editing request unless additional approval is specifically required.

docs.title: 2.1 Captions
docs.text:
1. Import the video into CapCut.
  2. Generate captions.
  3. Correct obvious transcription errors.
  4. Apply the Lynch Team caption format.
  5. Search the CapCut template for the all-caps blue text with white highlight style.
  6. Apply the style consistently.
  7. Reposition captions within the lower-third safe area.
  8. Ensure captions do not cover Dimitrios or important visual information.

docs.title: 2.2 Lynch Team Branding
docs.text:
1. Add The Lynch Team lion logo.
  2. Apply the required logo animation.
  3. Adjust the logo scale.
  4. Position the logo appropriately.

docs.title: 2.3 Additional Video Elements
docs.text:
Add the following when applicable:

  • Progress border - Required for videos that will be used for Stories, to make clip order easy to verify.
  • Location text - Add when relevant to the video's location/SEO context.
  • Other elements only when specifically required.

docs.title: 2.4 Audio
docs.text:
1. Normalize the audio volume.
  2. Apply minimal noise reduction when necessary.
  3. Preserve Dimitrios' original voice and delivery.

docs.title: 2.5 Thumbnail
docs.text:
1. Use the AI-generated thumbnail suggestions as the basis for the thumbnail.
  2. Select an appropriate video frame.
  3. Apply the established Lynch Team thumbnail format.
  4. Keep the thumbnail clear and natural.
  5. Save the finished thumbnail.

docs.title: 2.6 Export
docs.text:
1. Review the finished edit.
  2. Confirm all required elements are present.
  3. Export the final video.

Do Not

Do not add unnecessary transitions, effects, music, cuts, restructuring, or other creative edits unless specifically instructed.

docs.title: 3. AI Social Media Content
docs.text: Use the finalized CapCut captions/transcript to generate the complete social media content package.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Extract the captions/transcript from CapCut.
  2. Copy the transcript into the standard AI content-generation prompt.
  3. Generate the complete content package.
  4. Proofread the output.
  5. Correct errors or unsupported statements before publishing.
  6. Use the appropriate section of the generated package for each platform.

docs.title: Standard AI Prompt
docs.text:
Turn the transcript below into a complete social media content package for The Lynch Team.

Follow this exact order:

  1. Title: Strong hook that grabs attention without being clickbait.
  2. Facebook: Concise, natural, value-driven caption with relevant hashtags.
  3. Instagram: Short, engaging caption optimized for Instagram with hashtags.
  4. TikTok: Very concise caption, not caption-heavy, with relevant hashtags.
  5. TikTok First Comment: One natural question designed to encourage engagement.
  6. YouTube Titles: 3 SEO-friendly title options.
  7. YouTube Description: Detailed but readable, optimized for YouTube SEO, with hashtags.
  8. YouTube Tags: Relevant search keywords.
  9. Thumbnails: 5 options. Each should summarize the video in 1 to 2 lines, be clear and natural, and avoid clickbait/ad-like language.
  10. On-Screen Title: 3 options, maximum 6 to 8 words each. Make them strong hooks.
  11. Cleaned Transcript: Clean grammar, remove filler/repetition, but preserve Dimitrios' original meaning, voice, and facts. Do not add information.

Important rules:

  • Optimize caption length for each platform. Do not make every caption long.
  • Keep the Lynch Team tone professional, conversational, knowledgeable, and authentic.
  • Use hashtags where appropriate.
  • Never use em dashes or long hyphens. Use commas, periods, or parentheses instead.
  • Keep each section separate and copy-paste ready.
  • Do not combine sections.
  • Do not invent facts, claims, statistics, or details not supported by the transcript.

docs.title: 4. Notion Social Media Planner
docs.text:
1. Open the Lynch Team Social Media Planner.
  2. Locate the video based on its assigned date.
  3. Confirm the status is Not Started before publishing.
  4. Complete the editing and publishing workflow.
  5. Change the status to Completed after the video has been successfully published.

docs.title: Status Definitions
docs.text:
Status Meaning Not Started Video has not yet been published Completed Video has been successfully published

Planner: Lynch Team Social Media Planner

docs.title: 5. Facebook and Instagram
docs.text:
Tool: Meta Business Suite

  1. Upload the final edited video.
  2. Select Facebook and Instagram.
  3. Add the appropriate platform-specific caption generated by AI.
  4. Add the thumbnail/cover where applicable.
  5. Add location information when applicable.
  6. Review the post.
  7. Publish or schedule according to the Notion date.
  8. Confirm successful publication.

docs.title: 6. TikTok
docs.text:
Tool: GoHighLevel Social Planner

Important

Do not upload videos directly through TikTok. Direct TikTok uploads are currently avoided because they affect the intended audience location.

docs.title: Required Process
docs.text:
1. Upload the final video to GoHighLevel Media Storage.
  2. Open the GHL Social Planner.
  3. Create the TikTok post.
  4. Add the AI-generated TikTok caption.
  5. Add the TikTok First Comment where supported/applicable.
  6. Add the appropriate thumbnail/cover where available.
  7. Schedule or publish through GHL.
  8. Confirm successful publication.

GHL is the required publishing method for TikTok.

docs.title: 7. YouTube
docs.text: Tool: YouTube Native Uploader

docs.title: Video Classification
docs.text:
• 3 minutes or less: Publish as a YouTube Short.
  • Over 3 minutes: Publish as a regular YouTube video.

docs.title: Process
docs.text:
1. Upload the final edited video.
  2. Select one of the AI-generated YouTube titles.
  3. Add the AI-generated YouTube description.
  4. Add the AI-generated YouTube tags.
  5. Upload the thumbnail.
  6. Review the video details.
  7. Publish or schedule according to the Notion date.
  8. Confirm successful publication.

Tip

YouTube metadata is generated during the AI content-generation step. No separate metadata-generation process is required.

docs.title: Requirement
docs.text:
Warning

Every video that is 3 minutes or less must also be posted to Stories.

docs.title: 8.1 Segment the Video
docs.text:
1. Determine the final video length.
  2. Divide the video into approximately 18 to 23 second clips, depending on the total video length.
  3. Keep all clips in chronological order.
  4. Use the progress border added in CapCut as the visual cue for verifying clip order.

docs.title: 8.2 Publish Stories
docs.text:
Tool: Meta Business Suite

  1. Upload the Story clips.
  2. Confirm the clips are in the correct order.
  3. Use the progress border to verify the sequence.
  4. Review the complete Story sequence.
  5. Publish/schedule the Stories.

docs.title: 9. Temporary Storage
docs.text:
Storage: Google Drive

Google Drive is currently used as temporary storage to avoid consuming OneDrive storage.

docs.title: Upload
docs.text:
• Raw video
  • Final edited video
  • Thumbnail
  • Story clips, when applicable

Storage Folder: Lynch Team Google Drive Social Media Folder

docs.title: Storage Rule
docs.text: Maintain the files in the designated Google Drive folder until the team's future file-retention process determines when temporary files should be removed.

docs.title: 10. Final Quality Check
docs.text: Before marking the Notion item Completed, verify:

docs.title: Video
docs.text:
• Final video exported
  • Captions correctly formatted
  • Captions positioned in safe area
  • Lynch Team lion logo added
  • Logo animation applied
  • Required location text added
  • Progress border added for Stories
  • Audio normalized
  • Minimal noise reduction applied
  • Thumbnail created

docs.title: Content
docs.text:
• AI content package generated
  • Facebook caption reviewed
  • Instagram caption reviewed
  • TikTok caption reviewed
  • TikTok First Comment prepared
  • YouTube title selected
  • YouTube description reviewed
  • YouTube tags reviewed

docs.title: Publishing
docs.text:
• Facebook published
  • Instagram published
  • TikTok published through GHL
  • YouTube published
  • Stories published when video is 3 minutes or less

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
• Raw video uploaded
  • Final video uploaded
  • Thumbnail uploaded
  • Story clips uploaded when applicable

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: • Notion status changed from Not Started to Completed

docs.title: 11. Escalation Rule
docs.text:
Stop and notify Dimitrios when:

  • The video file is missing or corrupted.
  • The video appears incomplete.
  • Required information cannot be determined from the video/transcript.
  • AI-generated content contains information that cannot be verified from the transcript.
  • A platform prevents publication.
  • GHL cannot publish to TikTok.
  • A publishing issue may affect audience/location targeting.
  • Any change outside the standard editing workflow appears necessary.

Danger

Do not improvise changes to Dimitrios' content or publishing strategy when the issue falls outside this SOP.

docs.title: Website Management
docs.text:
Owner: (add name) Last reviewed: (add date)

Standard Operating Procedure for maintaining The Lynch Team website.

docs.title: 1. Website Content Audit
docs.text:
• Review the website page-by-page to identify outdated, missing, or inconsistent information.
  • Check key website sections and reusable elements for accuracy and consistency.
  • Update outdated reviews, testimonials, and review placeholders.
  • Replace or update video testimonials when new content is available.
  • Update blog post listings to ensure the latest posts are displayed correctly.
  • Review headers and footers for outdated links, information, or branding.
  • Check website colors and visual elements to ensure they remain consistent with The Lynch Team branding.
  • Fix or update any other outdated website content identified during the review.

docs.title: 2. SEO and Social Sharing
docs.text:
• Review each page's meta title and meta description and update them when needed.
  • Check page metadata to ensure it accurately reflects the page content and target topic.
  • Update Open Graph information used when pages are shared on social media.
  • Create and add Open Graph images for pages that do not have an appropriate image.
  • Check that page titles, descriptions, and images display correctly when shared.

docs.title: 3. Website Publishing and Quality Check
docs.text:
• Review all completed website changes before publishing.
  • Verify that updated text, images, links, videos, and page elements are displaying correctly.
  • Publish approved website updates.
  • Review the live pages after publishing to confirm the changes went live correctly.
  • Check for broken links, missing images, formatting issues, or other visible problems.
  • Make corrections as needed and recheck the affected pages.

docs.title: Pre-Publish Checklist
docs.text:
Before publishing any website update:

  • Content reviewed and approved
  • Text, images, links, videos display correctly
  • Meta title and description updated
  • Open Graph image set
  • Branding consistent
  • No broken links
  • No missing images

docs.title: Post-Publish Checklist
docs.text:
After publishing:

  • Live page reviewed
  • Changes visible as intended
  • No formatting issues
  • No broken links or missing images
  • Corrections applied if needed
